summary_paragraph: A male patient with a history of COPD, chronic aortic arch thrombus, factor V Leiden, and chronic pain was admitted for shortness of breath and pleuritic chest pain following recent influenza and a prednisone taper. He had exacerbated symptoms after physical exertion and was found to have a stable aortic arch clot on CT imaging. The vascular team recommended no acute intervention. Pain was initially difficult to manage due to patient's request for IV narcotics, but after one dose of IV Dilaudid, he agreed to transition back to oral oxycodone. He remained hemodynamically stable with improved symptom control. He was transitioned to oral prednisone, continued on enoxaparin, and discharged home with instructions to complete his antibiotic and steroid tapers, use DuoNeb treatments, and attend a scheduled CT scan and follow-up visit. Tobacco cessation was discussed and acknowledged.
problems: Embolism and thrombosis of thoracic aorta
Personal history of venous thrombosis and embolism
